'''Miklós Bóna''' (born in [[Székesfehérvár]]) is an American mathematician of [[Hungary|Hungarian]] origin.

Bóna completed his undergraduate studies in [[Budapest]] and [[Paris]], then obtained his Ph.D. at [[MIT]] in 1997 as a student of [[Richard P. Stanley]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=18053}}</ref> Since 1999, he has taught at the [[University of Florida]], where in 2010 he was inducted to the Academy of Distinguished Teaching Scholars.<ref>University of Florida, [https://fora.aa.ufl.edu/Provost/IndependentFora/Academy-of-Distinguished-Teaching-Scholars Academy of Distinguished Teaching Scholars]</ref>

Bóna's main fields of research include the [[combinatorics]] of [[permutation]]s, as well as [[enumerative combinatorics|enumerative]] and [[analytic combinatorics]]. Since 2010, he has been one of the [[editors-in-chief]] of the [[Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]].<ref>[https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/about/editorialTeam Editorial Team], [[Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]], accessed 2013-06-03.</ref>
